summary.headline: Enviro Infra Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 60% YoY to Rs 363.8 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 20.58% from 28.56% and PAT to Rs 39.5 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 60% YoY to Rs 363.8 crore in Q2 FY27, while EBITDA excluding other income rose 16.3% to Rs 74.9 crore. Margins compressed on higher other construction and operating expenses, interest on the deferred Suyog Gurja acquisition payment, and renewable IPP profit reversals at consolidated level. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 2,000 crore and EBITDA margin guidance of about 21% for water, 15-18% for renewables, and about 19-20% consolidated. Working capital and borrowings rose sharply, with debt-to-equity guided to about 0.3x by year-end.

segments.name: Water and wastewater (standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone Q2 revenue Rs 267.13 crore with EBITDA margin of 24.38%, above the revised FY27 guidance of about 21%. Order book of Rs 3,439 crore (ETC Rs 2,106 crore, hybrid annuity Rs 300.6 crore, O&M Rs 987 crore as stated).

segments.name: Renewable energy
segments.commentary: Renewables contributed about 29% of consolidated H1 FY27 revenue; order book about Rs 3,340 crore. Margin guided at 15-18%; IPP profits to be recognised only after commissioning and IPP revenue start, with margin expansion expected from Q3 and Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs 2,000 crore maintained; management expects about Rs 1,300 crore in H2 after about Rs 700 crore in H1.
FY27 PAT expected around Rs 240-250 crore, per management in Q&A.
EBITDA margin guidance: about 21% for water and wastewater; 15-18% for renewables; about 19-20% consolidated (one answer cited 19-25%).
Operating cash flow expected positive by Q4 FY27 according to management, though H1 OCF was negative.
Debt-to-equity expected to be not more than 0.3x by end of FY27 (currently about 0.53x).
Unbilled receivables expected to be near nil by March 2027 on Namami Ganga projects; trade receivable days guided down, from 93 to 63 days in H1.
FY27 water and wastewater order inflow target of about Rs 2,500 crore; management says Rs 2,250 crore balance to be won this year.
capex_capacity: Suyog Gurja acquisition: Rs 311 crore total consideration; Rs 111 crore paid as first tranche, Rs 200 crore to be paid over the next two years, with interest on deferred payment charged to P&L.
Two Namami Ganga projects in Varanasi (45 MLD at Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyay Nagar, Rs 126.78 crore; 60 MLD at Lohakha, Rs 130.14 crore), combined about Rs 257 crore excl. GST including 15-year O&M.
Two Bangalore projects worth about Rs 220 crore moving through execution; management says on schedule, ahead of time.
Renewable: Tata Power Renewable LOI for 180 MW Parli wind EPC (about Rs 190 crore excl. GST, completion by March 2027); ARLE Energy LOI for 100 MW Ayanee wind EPC (Rs 228 crore excl. GST).
Cumulative 58 water and wastewater projects completed with 1,018 MLD treatment capacity.
HAM projects Mathura (construction complete, COD expected soon), Saharanpur (fourth milestone pending), Yamuna Nagar and Ambala/Amritsar nearing completion.
demand_pricing: Management attributes the margin fall to West Asia conflict driving input cost inflation, price escalation clauses only partly passing through costs.

Renewable order book about Rs 3,340 crore: solar Rs 111 crore, wind Rs 1,054 crore (as stated), and IPP Rs 956 crore plus Rs 190 crore maintenance (as stated in transcript; component figures unclear).
Namami Ganga funds ring-fenced in dedicated escrow for HAM projects; Amrut fund release delayed in some states due to local approvals and signatories.
Management says ZLD and treated-water reuse are priority; not currently active in ultra-pure water for semiconductors; data centre water work seen as adjacent to ZLD capability.
ESS (energy storage) order book of about 930 MWh from NTPC plus one acquired IPP project; majority expected complete by June 2027.
Order pipeline includes Namami Ganga projects in UP and Jharkhand, Urban Challenge Fund projects, and a few overseas bids.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall 800-900 bps YoY and what is the Rs 178 crore 'other construction and operating expenses' line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the line includes all project execution costs (manpower, wages, civil and labour costs, job work) alongside purchase cost; it offered to read purchase plus other construction costs together. Margins also reflect interest on the Suyog Gurja deferred payment and IPP profit reversals at consolidated level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected consolidated margin profile going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 21% for water and wastewater, 15-18% for renewables, and about 19-20% consolidated; renewable profitability expected to improve significantly in Q3 and Q4 as ETC execution ramps and IPP revenue starts.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the two Bangalore projects and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Both projects, worth about Rs 220 crore, are under execution on schedule. Management said H1 revenue of about Rs 700 crore met guidance, with Rs 1,300 crore expected in H2 to reach Rs 2,000 crore, and PAT of Rs 240-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive and why was it negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects OCF positive by Q4 FY27. H1 OCF was negative mainly due to Rs 57 crore rise in service concession receivables (recoverable over 15 years) and Rs 102 crore outflow from trade receivable days falling from 93 to 63 days.

qa_highlights.question: Peak debt level and debt-to-equity trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-equity is about 0.53x now and expected to be not more than 0.3x by FY27 end. Borrowings rose on HAM projects and IPP projects; short-term working capital lines expected to decline as cash flow eases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the order mix shift further towards renewables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said water and wastewater remains the core, with no expected decline in opportunities. It is pursuing higher-quality, single-ticket reuse and wastewater projects and will wait for good projects rather than lower profitability guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for O&M share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: O&M revenue is expected to stay at 3-4% of standalone revenue, possibly rising to about 5%; O&M order book is about Rs 987 crore and new HAM projects will add recurring revenue over 5-15 years.

risks_watch: Margin compression: consolidated EBITDA margin 20.58% vs 28.56% YoY; watch whether renewable IPP margin recovery in Q3-Q4 materialises.
Working capital and leverage: trade receivables Rs 321.8 crore vs Rs 155.3 crore at March 2026; borrowings up sharply; OCF negative in H1.
H2 revenue must roughly double H1 (about Rs 1,300 crore needed) to meet Rs 2,000 crore guidance.
Input cost inflation from West Asia conflict with partial pass-through under price-escalation clauses.
Amrut fund release delays and state-level approval issues.
Deferred Suyog Gurja payment (Rs 200 crore over two years) adds interest cost and a future cash outflow.
Management's H1 PAT figure and some numbers were unclear in the transcript; verify against the filed results before relying on them.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the water and wastewater franchise, FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 2,000 crore and the standalone margin, and said it would not lower profitability guidance to win orders. It was cautious on consolidated margins, which it attributed to West Asia input-cost inflation, Suyog Gurja deferred-payment interest and IPP profit reversals, and it was evasive on the Rs 178 crore other construction and operating expenses line, offering to read it together with purchase cost instead of giving a breakup.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Mathura HAM COD expected soon, Parli 180 MW wind EPC completion by March 2027 and Ayanee 100 MW wind EPC (Rs 228 crore excl. GST) at LOI stage; Varanasi plants (Rs 257 crore combined) under construction, though 'capacity' here is project delivery rather than plant capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 2,000 crore held only with a 1.8x H2 ramp, and PAT guidance was cut to Rs 240-250 crore, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 must deliver about Rs 1,300 crore after Rs 723 crore in H1, PAT guide already cut, and consolidated margin fell to 20.58% amid West Asia input-cost inflation with partial price-escalation pass-through.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ESS order book of about 930 MWh from NTPC is expected to be mostly complete by June 2027, and ZLD / treated-water reuse is a stated priority, but no specific new product launch was named.

rows.label: Operating cash flow turns positive by Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management expects OCF positive by Q4 after negative H1, with trade receivable days guided down from 93 to 63 and unbilled receivables near nil by March 2027; receivables still rose to Rs 321.8 crore from Rs 155.3 crore.

rows.label: Debt-to-equity to 0.3x by FY27 end
rows.why: D/E currently about 0.53x with borrowings at Rs 703.9 crore, so getting to 0.3x requires a sharp cash-flow turn and Rs 200 crore Suyog Gurja deferred payment over two years still to be paid.

rows.label: Water order inflow of Rs 2,500 crore in FY27
rows.why: Rs 3,439 crore water order book exists and management says Rs 2,250 crore balance is to be won this year, with Namami Ganga UP/Jharkhand and Urban Challenge Fund projects in pipeline.
